keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has nothing before 1653. In August 1637 the Dutch took Elmina from the Portuguese and the table also lists Cape Coast Castle as occupied 1637-1652. The growth to Shama (1640), Anomabu (1640-52), Axim, Accra and Sekondi (1642) and Egya (1647) is carried by the ledger.

3,446 km2, 17 cells from Axim (2.5 W) to Accra (0.3 W), i.e. the fort sites then held: Axim, Shama, Elmina, Moree, Sekondi and Accra (the ledger dates each). The infobox gives no area, so no ratio. Temporary Dutch posts on the Ankobra (Ruychaver 1654-59, burned 1660) are not drawn.

4,021 km2: two cells added near 0.95-1.0 W, 5.2-5.3 N, east of Cormantin (Fort Amsterdam, 'captured in 1665 by Engel de Ruyter'; Fort Egya was Dutch 1647-1664); Cliopatria dates the step to 1670. Fort Witsen at Takoradi is also Dutch from 1665 and Fort Goede Hoop at Senya Beraku from 1667, which this shape does not obviously add.
4,394 km2: the cell set is the same as in 1670 and only the outline is finer; the nearest event is Fort Vredenburgh at Komenda ('The fort was built in 1682').

4,250 km2: one cell at 2.46 W differs from the 1683 shape. The page dates Fort Dorothea (Akwidaa) 'First occupied by the Dutch in 1687' (Brandenburger page: occupied 1687-1698), but Cliopatria adds the Akwidaa cells only in 1691.
4,825 km2: three cells added around 2.0-2.1 W, 4.9-5.0 N, the Akwidaa side where Fort Dorothea stood (Dutch 1687-1698); Fort Orange at Sekondi was enlarged in 1690.

4,882 km2: two cells at 2.5 W differ from 1691. The Komenda Wars (1694-1700) are 'a series of wars' in which 'little territory changed hands' (Komenda Wars page); Fort Orange at Sekondi was destroyed by the Ahanta in 1694 and restored afterwards.

4,221 km2: the Akwidaa cells go (Dutch occupation of Fort Dorothea ended in 1698 per the Brandenburger page) and four cells appear at 0.4-0.8 W, 5.3-5.6 N, the Apam side where Fort Lijdzaamheid was founded in 1697.

6,060 km2: seven cells return around Akwidaa and Princess Town: Fort Dorothea 'finally bought in 1721' and Fort Hollandia 'bought in 1721 by the Dutch' from Prussia. The Dutch could occupy Hollandia only in 1724 ('Up until 1724 occupied by the local Jan Conny').
6,089 km2: the cell set is unchanged from 1721; no event of 1727 on the page.

6,118 km2: one cell near Accra (0.35 W, 5.78 N) differs; no event of 1744 on the page. Fort Singelenburgh at Keta (1734-1737) was too short-lived and too far east to be in the shape. The infobox gives no area.

region.text: Fort Nassau at Moree

ledger.note: 1612: the Dutch build Fort Nassau at Moree, the first Dutch fort on the Gold Coast. 'In 1612, after gaining permission of the local rulers through the Treaty of Asebu, he built Fort Nassau'; infobox 'Established: 1612'. The fort table adds a first trading post around 1598.

region.text: Cape Coast Castle, 'Temporarily Occupied Forts' 1637-1652

ledger.note: 1637: the table lists Cape Coast Castle as occupied from 1637 (to 1652) with no remark; the page does not say from whom it was taken, so the counterpart is recorded as nobody.

region.text: Fort Elmina (St George) and Fort Coenraadsburg

1637: the capital moves from Fort Nassau at Moree to Elmina, which it stays until 1872 (infobox: Fort Elmina 1637-1872).

region.text: the Dutch forts east of Elmina

ledger.note: 1868: the forts east of Elmina pass to Britain. The treaty was signed 5 March 1867, effective 1 January 1868; Netherlands gave up Accra (Crevecoeur, renamed Fort Ussher), Moree (Nassau), Kormantin (Amsterdam), Senya Beraku (Goede Hoop) and Apam (Lijdzaamheid); 'all forts on the Gold Coast to the east of Elmina were to be handed over to Britain' (expedition page).

region.text: the British forts west of Elmina

ledger.note: 1868: the British forts west of Elmina pass to the Netherlands: Beyin (Apollonia, now Fort Willem III), Dixcove (Fort Metalen Kruis), Komenda and Sekondi, effective 1 January 1868. The Komenda king was deposed and the Dutch took the fort by force in February 1868 (expedition page).

region.text: Komenda, Kwassie and the villages around Elmina

ledger.note: 1868: resistance at Komenda. Treaty page: residents refused to raise the Dutch flag; expedition page: after the Komenda king approved the handover and was deposed, 'Dutch forces took the fort by force' in February 1868; the Fante Confederacy (formed January 1868 at Mankessim) besieged Elmina in April-May 1868 (Dutch page).

region.text: Komenda, Kwassie and the villages around Elmina

ledger.note: 1870: the Dutch punitive expedition ends. 'December 1869 and January 1870: A Dutch-led force burned the villages of Komenda, Anoema, and Kwassie'; an Ashanti army had reached Elmina on 27 December 1869. The page gives no peace date; the Dutch sold the colony in 1871-72.

wars.name: Battle of Elmina (1637)
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: Elmina captured from the Portuguese in August 1637, ending Portuguese rule on the Gold Coast; Shama (1640) and Axim (1642) followed.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Dutch War (Guinea theatre)

union.text: Fort Egya, placed on Fort Amsterdam at Kormantin because the dossier puts Egya 'near Cormantin' and the gazetteer has no Egya

wars.outcome: The English took Axim and Egya in 1664; De Ruyter recaptured Dutch posts in early 1665 and took Fort Amsterdam at Cormantin; at Breda (31 July 1667) the Dutch kept Fort Cormantin.
wars.note: The Second Anglo-Dutch War page is thin on the Gold Coast; the fort-level dates are the Dutch page's table. War dates on that page: 4 March 1665 to 31 July 1667.

wars.name: Komenda Wars
wars.outcome: Four wars over Komenda; 'little territory changed hands'; the English came out with the main trade advantage and the Dutch kept Fort Vredenburgh.
wars.note: Dutch attacked at Komenda in February 1695; Dutch-English trade agreement early 1698; Takyi Kuma named king of Eguafo on 9 May 1700. No contest event: the page records no ground taken.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War (Gold Coast)

union.text: Fort Lijdzaamheid (Fort Patience) at Apam, 5.286 N 0.7281 W (Fort Patience page)

zones.text: the five Dutch forts east of Elmina

wars.outcome: Britain seized five Dutch forts in 1782 and the Dutch took Fort Sekondi; all forts went back to their pre-war owners under the Treaty of Paris of 1784.

wars.name: Ahanta War (1838)
wars.outcome: 'The disastrous Ahanta War led to a royal decree on 23 March 1838 that strengthened colonial government'; no territorial change recorded.
wars.note: The page dates only the decree; the start of the war is not given.

wars.name: Fante Confederacy siege of Elmina
wars.outcome: The confederacy's army marched on Elmina in March 1868, began the siege in April and lifted it in May; a peace treaty between the confederacy and Elmina followed in June 1868.

wars.name: Dutch Gold Coast expedition of 1869-70
wars.outcome: Dutch-led force burned the villages of Komenda, Anoema and Kwassie in December 1869 and January 1870; the Dutch won militarily but the expedition 'ended Dutch involvement on the Gold Coast'; the colony was sold to Britain in 1872.
wars.note: Hostages from the warship Amstel were taken at Komenda on 26 May 1869 and ransomed for 15,000 guilders.

certainty.note: A string of coastal forts with undefined hinterlands: Cliopatria's shape is a coastal strip of 17 to 86 cells around the fort sites and the pages give no boundary. The only line the pages draw is the 1867 treaty's split at Elmina (forts west to the Netherlands, forts east to Britain), and that divides fort sites, not land.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW. Starts 1653 but the page's infobox gives 1612 (Fort Nassau); two new keyframes 1612 and 1637 cover the earlier years (single fort cells, so a rendering agent should expect almost nothing visible). Three rows are wrong: (1) 1853-1860 includes three cells of the Danish coast that Britain bought in 1850; (2) 1861-1872 includes a block of 22 cells in Nigeria that no Dutch page supports; (3) 1868-1872 still contains the whole coast to Accra although the 1867 treaty (effective 1 January 1868) gave every fort east of Elmina to Britain. The 1788 step (+3,000 km2) is unexplained by any page; its Beyin cells were British until 1868. The corrections use place names the gazetteer lacks (Moree, Elmina, Axim, Shama, Butre, Komenda, Apam, Cormantin, Egya, Senya Beraku, Dixcove, Beyin, Akwidaa, Princess Town, Anomabu, Keta) - listed in the report. AREA. The Dutch page gives no area, so no infobox ratio could be computed; areas are fort-neighbourhood strips and are soft. PAGE BUDGET. 9 Dutch pages opened (Dutch Gold Coast, Komenda Wars, Treaty 1867, Second Anglo-Dutch War, 1869-70 expedition, Brandenburger, Swedish, Fante Confederacy, British Gold Coast) plus the shared Danish page. UNSETTLED. (a) Dates disagree on the Dutch page: table says British occupied five forts 1781-1785, prose 1782; the Treaty of Paris 1784 vs evacuation 1785/86; Fort Nassau 1598 vs 1612; Fante page says the Dutch sold in 1870, treaty page and Dutch page say the 1871 treaty and 6 April 1872 handover (1872 used). (b) The Dutch paid tribute to Ashanti from 1701 ('two ounces of gold per month'); it is not written as a vassal event in either dossier, because Elmina stayed Dutch-ruled (batch notes af-04-a; the Ashanti ledger has no dutch-gold-coast event) [corrected by reviewer af-04-a].
